item.title: Salsa Thursdays at Time Out Market — Thu Aug 27, 7:00 PM — Time Out Market New York
item.description:
Join us for one of NYC’s best free salsa nights and turn your Thursday into a dance-floor celebration.
Get your salsa on every Thursday night at Time Out Market New York! Head up to the fifth floor for an electrifying evening of rhythm, movement, and Latin vibes. Whether you’re a total beginner or a seasoned dancer, this is your weekly excuse to move, sweat, and smile. Starting at 7:30 PM, renowned instructor Marlene Veras will guide you through the steps, breaking down the fundamentals so you feel confident on the dance floor. The night is powered by infectious beats from DJ Ray Suave, with live percussion by Jessica La Timbalera, setting the stage for a high-energy salsa experience. After the lesson, the floor opens up for a full-on salsa dance party until 10 PM. Bring a partner or come solo—everyone’s welcome.
Source: Go Latin Dance

item.description:
Join us for our last edition of BEDA · Put Trouble On My Tab!
BEDA series is dedicated to the people who keep the city’s cultural and hospitality scene alive: musicians, restaurant workers, and tourism professionals who rarely get to experience the events they help make possible. This five-month series offers a late performance on Sundays, so those who work weekends can finally enjoy world-class live music. The project also builds a cultural bridge between Toronto and Montreal, inviting exceptional artists from across provinces to share the stage and strengthen connections within Canada’s music ecosystem
MARZOS & MATEO, winners of the 18th edition of the Syli d'Or World Music Competition and recipients of the Afropop Worldwide Award 2025, present a concert rooted in their Latin American origins and Afro-Caribbean heritage, combining original compositions with salsa classics.

Join me in Toronto to launch “The Campfire Method” Come experience what warming up a room without awkward icebreakers actually feels like.
ABOUT THE EVENT This is not a book reading. It’s an intentionally designed experience. Most book launches are a reading and a Q&A. This one isn’t, mostly because it would make no sense. The Campfire Method is about designing genuine connection in a group, so I’m going to do that rather than describe it. You’ll walk in, and within a few minutes you find yourself in conversation with a like-minded person. Not through forced fun. Not through a round of two…

item.description: John Wilson emigrated from Scotland to the Prairies in 1912, joined the Royal North-West Mounted Police (RNWMP) and fell in love with a Canadian woman named Jessie. Then, his wife, Mary, whom he had abandoned in Scotland along with his children, unexpectedly showed up in Saskatchewan. Mary soon disappeared and Wilson went from Mountie to murder suspect. Author and freelance journalist, Nate Hendley, takes a look at a Canadian true-life murder mystery on the Prairies involving a double-crossing police officer, providing a glimpse behind the carefully polished image of the Mounties, to reveal a duplicitous liar who tried to get away with murder. item.title: Compute Runs on Minerals: Mapping AI’s Critical Mineral Exposure in the Age of Pax Silica — Tue Sep 15, 6:15 PM — https://luma.com/event/evt-C9UC5Ur3ANr8SF9
item.description:
Address: Check event page for more details.
Every frontier model runs on minerals. Behind the GPUs, the servers, the cooling systems and the power infrastructure that make up a data centre sit gallium, germanium, rare earths, copper, tungsten and a dozen other inputs whose mining and refining are concentrated in a small number of countries. Countries like China, that have weaponized that dominance, restricting exports of gallium, germanium, graphite and rare earth magnets, and each time targeting a material critical to AI. Demonstrating how a supply chain chokepoint becomes a tool of statecraft.
What exactly is AI infrastructure,…
Hosted by Georgia Berg
Source: Luma Toronto Discover

London: A Guide for Curious Wanderers London: Hidden Corners for Curious Wanderers About the Books London is famous for its museums, each one full of treasures and relics – but the biggest museum in the capital is the city itself. From the stories behind unusual street names, to the trees in our parks; railings made from recycled WWII stretchers, to shrapnel damage on walls; the hidden symbols on post boxes, to prehistoric tree trunks – there is a rich history hidden in the oft-overlooked details of the city's streets, gardens, parks and buildings. This richly detailed and beautifully illustrated book provides a miscellany of historic features and curiosities to spot as you wander around the capital.
